posts.title: Tu Mil Jaaye meets its first boycott call
posts.deck: A Delhi BJP MLA wants Deepika Padukone's orange-outfit sequence cut from KING's first song. The song kept climbing: 68.4 million YouTube views on its eighth day.

blocks.p: KING's first song has its first political fight. BJP MLA Ravi Negi, who represents Delhi's Patparganj constituency, has demanded that the makers remove the sequence in Tu Mil Jaaye in which Deepika Padukone dances with Shah Rukh Khan in an orange outfit, and has called for a nationwide boycott of the film if they do not, Moneycontrol and The Telegraph reported on 6 and 7 November.

quote.q: If Shah Rukh Khan does not remove the bhagwa scene, we will call for a nationwide boycott of King.
quote.by: Ravi Negi, BJP MLA, speaking to Dainik Samachar (as quoted by Moneycontrol, 7 Nov 2026)

blocks.p: In the same interview Negi called the actor a "Jihadi", Moneycontrol and The Daily Star reported. On 7 November Ayodhya's Mahant Sitaram Das Maharaj told ANI that a dance in saffron "would not be tolerated" and suggested the actress wear green instead, according to Bhaskar English.

The row repeats December 2022, when Deepika Padukone's saffron outfit in Besharam Rang, a song from Pathaan, drew protests and a threatened ban in Madhya Pradesh. Siddharth Anand, who directs KING, said then that the colour was chosen for the song's sunny backdrop. Pathaan opened in January 2023 and went on to become one of the highest-grossing Hindi films of all time. MovieTalkies summed up this week's echo: same colour, same actress, same actor, same director.

On social media, fans answered the boycott call with jokes and reels, iDiva reported. Red Chillies Entertainment kept posting: a full-version streaming link on 8 November, Diwali wishes the same evening and, this morning, two posts for 19 years of Om Shanti Om, the film that first paired Shah Rukh Khan and Deepika Padukone, each signed off "#KING in cinemas on 24.12.2026".

posts.title: Agar Main King Hota: the final mix, and sheet music for every fan
posts.deck: The final version of the site's song is out, 6 minutes and 49 seconds, with a new poster of the King and his saxophone, and free sheet music for every instrument.

blocks.p: A day after its release, Agar Main King Hota has its final mix. The song, created by Shailja Gupta using Claude, ChatGPT and Suno, now plays on the site in its finished form, with a new poster, the lyrics as they are sung, and sheet music that anyone can download for free.

The new poster puts the King on a bridge at night, in the rain, a saxophone at his lips and a red crown above his head. Its line reads 'Based on SRK's Real Tech Career': the song is a documentary of that career, from Aryan Infomatics and SRKWorld to Little G.ONE.
The saxophone is the King's instrument in the song too. It carries the long break at 2:57 and returns before the bridge, answering the voice where the violin used to.

Every instrument has its own sheet: vocals, alto sax in E♭, violin, guitar, bass and drums, plus a full score for a conductor. Each comes as a PDF to print, a MusicXML file to open in MuseScore, Sibelius or Finale, and a MIDI file to hear the part. A band, a school or a fan with a guitar can play the whole song from them, at no cost.

quote.by: Agar Main King Hota, the last line, sung twice

blocks.p: The lyrics on the song page now follow the recording line by line, with every chorus, instrumental and the bridge marked. The song closes on 'Agar main tu hota', almost whispered and sung twice, a line left for the King himself.

posts.title: Agar Main King Hota: the song is out
posts.deck: The site's own song, created by Shailja Gupta, is out today: six minutes and 47 seconds of a fan's India, from Bombay to Ladakh, that ends in one line, 'Agar main tu hota'.

blocks.p: Agar Main King Hota, the song this site is named after, was released on Friday 6 November. It was created by Shailja Gupta, using Claude, ChatGPT and Suno, and it plays in full on the site from today.

blocks.h: A map of India, line by line

blocks.p: The song opens on a single question and then walks the country, one city to a line: Bombay is home, Madras the Taj Mahal, Calcutta the adda, Dilli the sky, Kashmir destiny, Darjeeling the fog. A second verse goes on to Lucknow, Banaras, Amritsar, Punjab, Hyderabad, Kerala, Goa, Kanyakumari and Ladakh. Every line ends the same way, 'hota': what would be, if.

quote.q: Chehra mera, sirf mera hi hota, / Awaaz meri, par naam sirf tera hota

blocks.p: Halfway through, the song stops being a king's wish list. The face and the voice become the subject, the same fight the fans' anthem INQUILAAB KING KE SAATH took up on 28 October: a star's face, voice and name belong to him. Then comes the confession of a fan, and a last verse that drops the crown altogether.
It ends quietly, on 'Agar main tu hota': if I were you.

posts.title: Ramayana's first day: ₹64.85 crore
posts.deck: Ramayana: Part 1 opened at ₹64.85 crore net in India, according to Sacnilk. Jawan's ₹75 crore opening day is still the mark KING is chasing on 24 December.

blocks.p: Ramayana: Part 1 opened on Thursday 5 November, in five languages. By the end of the night, the first-day numbers were in.

Kannada (₹7.25 crore), Telugu (₹6.00 crore), Tamil (₹2.60 crore) and Malayalam (₹1.50 crore) make up the rest. Bollywood Hungama reports the opening day at ₹62.50 crore. Overseas: N/A, not yet reported.
Ramayana sold more tickets in advance than Jawan, but Jawan's first day is still higher. Advance booking is a promise. Day one is the walk-in crowd.

KING opens in 48 days, on 24 December, Christmas Eve. The two numbers to watch are now set: the Hindi opening-day record and the ₹75 crore that Jawan put up in 2023. Ramayana's run over the Diwali weekend will show how big this season's audience is.

posts.title: Tu Mil Jaaye: 1 lakh reels in four days, #1 on Instagram
posts.deck: KING's first song has crossed 1 lakh reels on Instagram in under four days and is trending at #1. By 09:20 IST this morning the count stood at 117,000.

blocks.p: Tu Mil Jaaye, the first song from KING, has crossed 1 lakh reels on Instagram in less than four days and is trending at number one on the platform, Team Shah Rukh Khan, SRK's official fan club, announced at 09:01 IST on Friday. Twenty minutes later, the song's audio page on Instagram stood at 117,000 reels.
The 117,000 counts only reels made with the official audio. Reels set to fan re-uploads of the song sit on separate audio pages, so the full number is higher.

Views count people who watched. Reels count people who made something with the song: a dance, a lip-sync, a couple's video, a fan edit. In four days, more than a lakh fans put KING's first song into their own videos, 48 days before the film opens on 24 December.

posts.title: Ramayana opens, and the season begins
posts.deck: Ramayana: Part 1 is in cinemas today with the second-biggest opening-day advance booking ever reported for a Bollywood film. KING follows on 24 December.

blocks.p: Diwali week, Thursday 5 November 2026. Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1, produced by Namit Malhotra, with Ranbir Kapoor as Ram, Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita, opened in cinemas this morning.

stats: Tickets sold before the first show

blocks.p: As reported by Sacnilk at 10:08 IST, that is the second-highest opening-day advance booking for a Bollywood film, behind Dhurandhar 2 (₹52.35 crore) and ahead of Jawan (₹40.75 crore). Koimoi reports it as the highest ever for a film that is not a sequel. These are reported pre-sales, not box office.

stats: still being counted; the final figure is due tomorrow

blocks.p: Live trackers were showing different day-one numbers through the morning, so we print N/A until a final figure is reported.

list: Hindustan Times: 4 stars (as reported by Marksmen Daily)

blocks.p: The common thread: the scale, the visual effects and Yash's Ravana are praised; the slow first half and the music divide the critics. Part 1 builds the world. The battle is saved for Part 2.

Ramayana's pre-sales passed Jawan's. The bar for a big Hindi opening has just been raised, 49 days before KING opens on 24 December. This season is a relay, not a clash: Ramayana at Diwali, KING at Christmas.

posts.title: Agar Main King Hota, and how the King turned 61
posts.deck: What this fans' KING world is, and the story so far: from the song at midnight on his birthday to a 24-hour record.
posts.img_alt: Tu Mil Jaaye, released the minute he turned 61

blocks.h: What Agar Main King Hota is

blocks.p: Agar Main King Hota, if I were the King, is the question every Shah Rukh Khan fan has asked at least once. This site is where the fans answer it: a fan-built world around KING, Shah Rukh Khan's film that opens on 24 December 2026. Not a campaign you watch; one you enter.

Asoka to Boo-Da: the book, SRK: The Man, The Myth, The King; plus the Gallery, On The Record and Character Study

blocks.p: Everything here is made by fans, for fans, and every number is one we read ourselves. SRK DAILY is where we write it up, every day, until KING and beyond.
Shah Rukh Khan vs. the clock. Toss won by the King, elected to bat at midnight.

time: No balcony. The man who has waved from Mannat almost every birthday since 2007 sent a handwritten note instead, lit across the scaffolding of his own home: "Thank you all for your wishes and love. Sending mine right back to you all. Lots of love and a big hug."

First ball. KING's first song, Tu Mil Jaaye, drops on YouTube the minute he turns 61. Sachin-Jigar, Kumaar, Arijit Singh, Madhubanti Bagchi, and Ed Sheeran in a Hindi film song. Shah Rukh and Deepika on screen.
His own post: "Of Love and other Battles... This December, #LoveLikeAKing"

blocks.p: We read the YouTube counter every 10 minutes, all day.
His Instagram reel, same 22 hours 55 minutes: 1.3 million likes, 62,100 comments, 51,000 shares.

5,000+ fans in Mumbai (an SRK Universe fan-club estimate, via PTI). Police barricades 500 metres from his gate. Fans screening DDLJ, feeding an orphanage, running free health check-ups. The Burj Khalifa saying "WE LOVE YOU SRK". The Bandra-Worli Sea Link carrying his face the night before.

After skipping the balcony in 2024 and 2025, and with Mannat wrapped in scaffolding, he walked out anyway. White T-shirt, beanie, a platform built just for the moment. Waved. Bowed. Folded his hands. Opened his arms.
Late night, the party outside Mannat went on, and he came back out. Kisses blown, the signature pose, the street singing his name.
3 November, 17:26 IST, 41 hours 17 minutes in: 41,796,168 views and 500,181 likes. Half a million likes before the second sunset. By 21:15 IST: 43,451,423 views.
Day one ran at about 1.5 million views an hour. Day two settled at about 357,000 an hour, the normal second-day curve for a song that has already been everywhere.

The fans did the rest. In three days we counted 127 new YouTube videos about the song and the birthday (reactions, reviews, covers, remixes, AI versions) and 176 fan-made posts on Instagram and X, each checked by hand.

And the season's scoreboard moved too. KING's two official teasers together had 84,010,198 YouTube views, past the Avengers: Doomsday trailer's 83,646,111. Ramayana: Part 1 opens on 5 November; all seven of its official videos add up to 127,204,303 views. KING's three: 127,528,651. Dead level, 51 days before KING opens.

Hindustan Times, Bollywood Hungama and UNI report, from the makers' own numbers, that Tu Mil Jaaye became the most-watched Indian film song on YouTube in its first 24 hours: 36.3 million views and 430,000 likes, past Zinda Banda from Jawan (34.6 million, as reported). That is the makers' figure as carried by the press, not a post from @iamsrk or @redchilliesent.

Our own log agrees with it. We read the public YouTube counter every 10 minutes on his birthday: 35,243,482 views and 416,961 likes at 23:04 IST, 22 hours 55 minutes after release. UNI and DNA also report more than 60 million views across all digital platforms in a day; we only count YouTube.
On agarmainkinghota.com, the fans' own KING campaign, we publish KING's buzz in public every day against a fixed baseline. Real numbers only; if we can't read it, it says N/A.
